During the time of meditation, one must not listen to Purāṇas or other such texts.
A wise person should perform meditation in solitude with eyes closed. (53)
The hearing of the Purāṇas and other scriptures occurs during the consecration and not otherwise;
endowed with firmness of mind and steadfast in his vows, he should worship me.
Viṣṇu is fond of ornaments, I am fond of consecration,
the Sun is fond of salutations, and my attendants are fond of hymns of praise.
(68) The recitation of hymns especially increases my joy; by the mere recitation of a hymn, I am satisfied and bestow the desired fruit. (56)
Through meditation, all evil is destroyed, as well as that which is earned through devotion;
other practices are secondary to meditation, for meditation alone is proclaimed as the primary means. (57)
Having prepared two golden basins filled with pure water and mixed with fragrant substances, one should worship me.
Cardamom, cloves, nutmeg, fruits and flowers, uśīra, clove bark, jaṭāmāṃsī, takkola, and kuṣṭha. (59)
The root of the Kadamba, fragrant bark, Nāgakeśara, Campaka, Devadāru, Guggulu, and saffron flowers as well. || 60 ||
Having ground together equal parts of gorocana, camphor, and all types of gems, one should especially add musk; then,
having placed all these substances [within], one should worship him in the form of a liṅga.
When all ritual substances are unavailable, one should procure camphor mixed with musk and saffron for the sake of worship and perform the adoration;
if one is poor and lacks cardamom and ushira root, one should worship with pure water alone.
To whatever extent the ritual equipment for my worship is distinguished, to that same extent the fruit is proclaimed; for devotees, there is indeed no sin. (63)
A devotee should perform the waving of lights with lamps made of gold or silver;
he should offer them along with flowers for the sake of attaining the perfection of his own spiritual knowledge. (64)
The attainment of knowledge shall come to men by offering a lamp to me,
especially on Mondays and by the offering of a row of lamps.
By offering lamps on a Monday during the month of Kārttika,
a devotee shall not be born again, but shall attain union with me (sāyujya).
The fruit that arises from offering a hundred thousand lamps at dusk on a Monday cannot be described; it is certain that he [the Lord] himself is that fruit.
Therefore, one should perform the worship of lamps for the destruction of ignorance. 67.
One should perform eight prostrations, or one hundred and eight, or even a thousand; for I am fond of prostrations.
Having worshipped me, who am with Ambā and in the form of a Liṅga, upon the palm of the hand, the devotee should then perform a prostration, visualizing it as extending above the throat. (69)
O Great Goddess, having performed the rite of circumambulation with the fist and the thumb released, one should pray to me without weariness according to one's desire.
(70) Holding his lotus-like hands joined with the Unmanī-mudrā, he should also offer the *arghya*;
and with the Cid-mudrā, he should present the flowers and the vessels. (71)
Afterwards, one should cover [the deity] with an umbrella and also fan it with a chowrie;
likewise, one may also show a mirror and use a palm-leaf fan.
One should cause the sound of bells to be made and also blow the conch shell;
one should certainly have songs heard and offer instrumental music and dance.
The ritual for the house of worship:
The Śiva temple of worship should be pure, smeared with white lime, anointed with cow dung, and adorned with colored powders, garlands, and other ornaments. (74)
Having adorned it with flowers and leaves, one should spread out a *mallījhillī* canopy;
and one should fumigate the temple of the deity with powders of fragrant substances.
One should construct nests upon the wall that shimmer in various colors,
and one should quickly place my attendants (kiṅkaras) in their forms within them.
They were equipped with weapons and vehicles, adorned with ornaments,
their bodies radiant with ash, the triple-tilaka, and rudrākṣa beads, and they wore matted hair.
Alternatively, the wise one should place sacred ash and rudrākṣa beads in those nests; or else, he should arrange the materials for my worship there,
and he should also prepare a row of lamps in each of those respective nests.
O Goddess, having completed the rite of worship in that excellent hall, seated comfortably on an auspicious seat,
one should be adorned with the triple mark of ashes and a rosary of rudrākṣa beads.
Adorned with all the ritual implements arranged upon the Bhadrādimaṇḍala, having performed the ritual of sakalīkaraṇa upon his body, and having offered praise to the retinue of deities; || 80 ||
Having visualized an excellent, well-adorned lion-throne at the front, and having prepared a hand-pedestal there, elevated upon a bed of ashes; || 81 ||
Having placed me within that [liṅga] constantly with the thirty-six modes of service, as well as with the Ṛg, Yajur, and Sāma Vedas, and likewise with the mantras of the Atharvaveda; || 82 ||
By means of the *Pañcākṣara-upaniṣad*, by listening to the Purāṇas and so forth, by the study of the scriptures, and also by multitudes of hymns in prose and verse; || 83 ||
One should sing oneself and cause others to sing hymns indicative of my greatness;
one should satisfy me with various musical instruments, songs, and dances.
One should offer nine *ārārtika* lamps to me in a sequence beginning with one, accompanied by the sounds of the *jāghaṇṭā*, the conch, and even tumultuous clamor. (85)
Consisting of the bliss of the Word-Brahman (Śabdabrahman) and immersed in the nectar of my own bliss,
he was as if submerged in contentment, appearing unconscious yet entirely absorbed in that.
He who worships me himself, whether once or even repeatedly,
is blessed among all people, worthy of veneration, and the most excellent of supreme devotees;
and he who rejoices upon seeing him would be even greater than he.
He who, in his own home, constantly provides the materials for worship— especially for my devotees— and causes them to perform my worship with those materials,
attains union with me (sāyujya), which is difficult even for the wise to attain.
Thus have I spoken to you, O Goddess, for the sake of achieving liberation for the worlds; what more do you wish to hear regarding the placement of the vessels and other implements? 89.

Thus ends the fifth chapter, titled "The Description of the Characteristics of the Vessels for Worship and Other Items," in the Kriyāpāda of the Uttara-bhāga of the Śrī-Kāraṇāgama, within the dialogue between Pārvatī and the Supreme Lord. || 5 ||
The sixth chapter. The Goddess said:
O Moon-crested One, Lord of Beings, wielder of the Pināka bow, Ugra, Śaṅkara!
Please explain specifically the ritual procedure for the worship performed at the appropriate times and other such occasions. || 1 ||
Mahādeva said:
The Ritual for Occasional Worship.
Now, O beloved, I shall describe the ritual procedure for occasional worship; listen.
Having first envisioned the maṇḍala, one should then light a lamp.

Having received the permission of the assembly, preceded by the ringing of bells, and having sipped water while reciting my names, one should perform breath control (prāṇāyāma) according to one's ability. || 3 ||
Having proclaimed the place and time, one should properly worship the water-pot and recite my six-syllabled mantra at least one hundred and eight times.
One should place the *liṅga*—which is established as the embodiment of all signs—in the hand;
one should display it, saying "This is he," during the rite known as *nīrājana* (the waving of lights).
Having sprinkled with ashes while reciting, "He who is Rudra is indeed the Blessed One, the Earth," and while reciting, "Such is His greatness," one should offer water for the feet (*pādya*). (6)
One should offer the arghya with the verse "haṃsaḥ śuciṣat," the water for sipping (ācamanīyaka) with the Sāvitrī mantra, and the bath (snāna) with the formula "namaḥ somāya ca. || 7 ||
Having sprinkled the bathing water on his head and taken up the sacred water from the Linga-tirtha,
he should sip it while reciting "Ṛtaṃ Satyam," and put on his garment while saying "Yaḥ santu."

The wise one should smear ashes all over [the body] with the mantra beginning "Agniriti" (Taittirīya Āraṇyaka 10.37); he should take scents with the mantra "Gandheti" (Taittirīya Āraṇyaka 10.38) and unbroken rice-grains with the mantra "Ākāśāditi" (Taittirīya Āraṇyaka 10.39).
One should offer flowers with the mantra "Nidhanapataye," bilva fruit with "Tryambakam," and incense with "Yadvyoma."
One should perform the great lustration (*mahānīrājana*), recollecting the mantra "na tatra" [from the *Viṣṇu Purāṇa*];
one should offer the final dismissal (*avasara*) and the food offering (*naivedya*), as indicated by the signs of proper conduct and other such marks. (11)

One should offer the mantra-flower with the mantra "Īśānaḥ". One should perform the covering with a cloth using the mantra "So 'bravīt". And one should place the Liṅga upon one's own body with the mantra "Aṇor aṇīyān". || 12 ||
The Brief Ritual for Worship:
Now, O Goddess, I shall describe the brief ritual for worship; listen.
Having bathed, being pure and self-controlled, and having covered oneself with sacred ash— || 13 ||

Having applied the triple mark (tripuṇḍra), his body adorned with a rosary of rudrākṣa beads, having sipped water for purification (ācamana), lit the lamp, and offered prayers to my attendants (gaṇas); || 14 ||
Having sipped water, restrained the breaths, and proclaimed the place and time,
one should perform the worship of the desired Liṅga here with whatever materials are available.
Having made the resolve, "I shall do it," and having likewise worshipped the water-pot (kalaśa),
the wise man should perform the recitation of the six-syllable mantra one hundred and eight times.
Holding the chosen *liṅga* in his hand and reciting the mantra of all *liṅgas*, he should perform the invocation while saying, "I am the Veda; [the Lord] is to be grasped through devotion.
He should then display the *nīrājana* known as "darśana" (the vision), saying, "This is He. || 17 ||

Having sprinkled with ashes while reciting, "He who is Rudra is indeed the Blessed One, the Earth," and contemplating, "Such is his majesty," one should offer the water for washing the feet (pādya). || 18 ||

Having offered the arghya with the verse "haṃsaḥ śuciṣat," the water for sipping (ācamanīyaka) with the Sāvitrī mantra, and having performed the consecration (abhiṣeka) with the mantra "yo vai rudraḥ sa bhagavān āpaḥ."
Having taken hold of Liṅgatīrtha while reciting the mantra "kadrudrāya," and having sipped water while reciting "ṛtaṃ satyam," he offered flowers and incense.

"O beloved, having offered the *nīrājana* lamp known as 'the opportunity' (*avasara*) according to the mantra, 'He who is Rudra is indeed the Blessed Lord, and he who is Agni,' one should then provide the opportunity for fruits and other offerings, and cast sacred ash (*bhasma*) upon the *liṅga*."
O Dear One, having offered a flower with the root mantra, one should cause incense to be smelled while recollecting this mantra: "asau yo 'vasarpati.
O Daughter of the Mountain, one should then display the lustration known as the "bath" (majjana).
Reciting, "Such is his greatness," one should offer water for the feet (pādya);
with the mantra "haṃsaḥ śuciṣat" one should offer the arghya, and with the Sāvitrī mantra, the water for sipping (ācamanīyaka). || 23 ||
Performing the consecration with the Rudrādhyāya according to the mantra,
one should wipe [the face] with a cloth, take up the water from the Lingatīrtha,
and after consecrating it with the mantra "Kadrudrāya," one should consume it while reciting "Ṛtam. (24)
Reciting "Yo vai rudraḥ," one should offer the heating of charcoal;
reciting "Yo vai rudraḥ sa bhagavān yaścāgniḥ," one should offer incense.
Reciting "uddīpyasva," he should show the cloth called *māṅgalya*;
O Goddess, he should offer the garment while reciting the mantra beginning with "yastantu. (26)
One should offer the sacred ash along with water using the mantras beginning with "Agnis";
one should offer the sacrificial thread (yajñasūtra) with the mantra "Namo Harikeśāya. || 27 ||
Having recited "Yo vai Rudro yā ca Pṛthvī," one should offer perfumes along with unbroken rice grains; then, with the mantra "Ākāśāt," one should offer unbroken rice grains alone.
(78) One should offer the camphor lustration (nīrājana) with the words, "Pervading all," and having offered garlands with the words, "That very one is the support of the world. 29.
"O Rudra, that auspicious form of yours which is auspicious and a healing balm for all days"—
with these words, O Maheśvarī, one should offer the lustration rite (nīrājana) known as Śṛṅgāra.

One should offer flowers with the mantra "He who is Rudra is indeed the Blessed One, and he who is Sūrya," and so on in sequence; then with the mantra "To the Lord of the Nidhanas" repeated one hundred and eight times; and one should offer bilva leaves with the mantra "Tryambakam. (31)
One should offer a white umbrella with the words, "Obeisance to Īdhriya," and one should present a fly-whisk with the words, "Obeisance to Vātya. || 32 ||
One should offer a fan with the mantra, "The moon was born from the mind," and likewise one should offer a mirror with the mantra, "He who is this person here. (33)
Reciting "yo vedādau" and sounding the bell, one should likewise properly blow the conch shell with the mantra "adhyavocad adhivaktā. (34)
The wise one should cause [the deity] to hear the song with the words, "By auspicious speech, indeed" (p.
79). The discerning one should play musical instruments with the words, "Homage to Dundubhi.
And he should perform a dance with the words, "Homage to Rudra, the assailant" (namo rudrāyātatāyine). || 35 ||
With the mantra "udyantam," the wise man should perform a circumambulation;
reciting "yo rudro 'gnau," he should offer his salutation.
Having said "Salutation to Rudra," the wise man should recite the hymn of praise;
then, reciting the verse beginning with "ajāta," he should perform the act of supplication.
"Rudra is indeed the Blessed One, and that which is space is the incense;
'the sun does not shine there'—thus one should offer the great *nīrājana*. (38)
Then, with the mantra "aghorebhyo 'tha" and others, such as the ācāra-liṅga and so forth, the practitioner should subsequently offer the fourfold food offering (naivedya) in due order. || 39 ||
Having sprinkled ashes upon the great liṅga with the mantra "Īśāna," one should likewise offer the mantra-flower with the root mantra (mūlamantra). || 40 ||
Then, even while reciting the mantra, "From which words turn back," one should also offer the lustration rite (nīrājana) known as Ānanda.
Saying "He is Viśva" while offering betel-leaf, and saying "He who is Brahmā," he should scatter handfuls of flowers and offer even his own self.

One should perform the *asaṃkhya-nīrājana* with the mantra beginning "asaṃkhyā"; one should perform the covering with a cloth using the mantra "so 'bravīt"; and one should perform the placement [of the deity] upon one's own body with the mantra "aṇoraṇīyān. || 43 ||
Thus has been declared, O Great Goddess, the concise procedure for propitiation;
for this bestows union with Me upon those who practice it as prescribed. (44)

Thus ends the sixth chapter, titled "The Exposition of the Ritual of Worship," in the section on ritual action (*kriyāpāda*) within the dialogue between Pārvatī and the Supreme Lord (*Parameśvara*), in the latter part of the *Śrīkaraṇāgama*. || 6 ||
The seventh chapter. The Goddess said:
O God of gods, O Mahādeva, you who are intent upon the grace of the worlds!
O Lord of the Universe, by merely hearing of your worship, I have attained my life's purpose.
O sole cause of the world, I desire to hear about the great worship;
having enlightened me regarding its procedure, please favor me with your compassion. (2)
Mahādeva said:
O Great Goddess, I shall now describe the sequence of the procedure for the great worship (mahāpūjā).
Having bathed, being pure and restrained in mind, he put on a pair of washed garments.

Having applied the triple horizontal mark (tripuṇḍra), his body adorned with a rosary of rudrākṣa beads, having performed the twilight prayers (sandhyā) and other rites, and having prepared the necessary materials such as flowers; || 4 ||
Having placed the vessels for worship upon the Bhadradimaṇḍala and being seated on a comfortable seat,
he should light four— or indeed two— lamps.
Having recited the Gaṇas, sipped water (ācamana), and performed breath control (prāṇāyāma) in due order,
he should clearly proclaim the place and time for the propitiation of the desired deity.
Having placed the common arghya vessel upon the colored lines,
one should deposit pure ashes, sandalwood, and flowers therein.
Having filled it with water, one should contemplate it as being filled by a stream of nectar dripping from a single drop; then, having consecrated it with the Pañcabrahma and Ṣaḍaṅga mantras,
one should purify it with the rites that will be described hereafter.
Inspection, sprinkling, striking, veiling, and sprinkling with water—
these are known as the purifiers of the ritual substance.
Having rendered it nectar-like by means of the [mudrā] called Dhenu, one should display it upon the lotus-liṅga.
Then, one should arrange the vessels for the water for the feet (pādya), the respectful offering (arghya), and the water for sipping (ācamana) in rows;
to the north of those, one should place the vessel for the water for the feet in due order.
The best of practitioners should place siddhārtha seeds, saffron, dūrvā grass, kuṣṭha, camphor, ashes, sandalwood, and flowers [into the vessel]. || 11 ||
Having filled the water with the six limbs and consecrated it with the *sadyojāta* mantra,
one should likewise scatter *kuśa* grass and other items into the *arghya* vessel situated to its north.
Having sprinkled water with the *hṛdaya* mantra and consecrated it with the root mantra (*mūla*), one should place ashes and other substances into the *ācamana* vessel to its north.
Having filled it with water using the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*) mantras, one should consecrate it with the *sadyojāta* and other mantras. || 13 ||
One should also place the vessels for renunciation, knowledge, and bliss in front of that.
Having placed ashes, sandalwood paste, and flowers into the vessel of renunciation,
one should fill it with warm water and consecrate it with the Prāsāda mantra.
Then, having placed ashes and other substances in a vessel for knowledge to its north,
and having filled it with sandalwood water, one should consecrate it with the Aghora mantra.
Then, having placed ashes and other substances into the vessel of the subsequent bliss (uttarānanda),
and having filled it with cool water, one should consecrate it with the Vāmadeva mantra.
To the east of that, for the purpose of obtaining water from the bath and the foot-refreshment pavilion,
one should place three supporting vessels there in a row.
One should place the Śiva-kumbha in front of the general arghya vessel;
having poured ashes and so forth into it, one should then add the water for drinking.
One should fill [the vessels] with the heart mantra, saying "in the jars," and consecrate them with the mantra, "The waters indeed are all this. (19)
Having sprinkled the articles of worship with water drawn from that [vessel],
one should then worship the vessels for the general *arghya* and so forth with the root mantra.
Then, one should pour the water contained in the general *arghya* vessel into the three vessels for the *pādya* and the others.
Having worshipped the Guru with self-restraint by means of the mantra "yasya deva," one should receive the holy water and the sacred offerings (prasāda) in order to attain fitness for my worship.

Thus the stage of the devotee (bhaktasthala) has been described; now, in the stage of the Great Lord (māheśvarasthala), one should indeed perform the purification of the hands with the mantra: "This is my hand. (22)

Having performed the ritual worship of the Maheśvara-sthala with the mantra "sarvabhūtastham," and having taken the sacred ash for his seat with the mantra "kare," he took the linga from that house with the mantra "vedāhametam."
One who establishes the universal sign (sarvaliṅga) should place the sign in his hand.

Then one should perform the invocation with the mantra: "O Rudra, that which is your southern face. Having meditated upon the Guru and properly performed the six-limbed ritual placement (ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa), one should indeed recite the six-syllabled mantra either a thousand times or six hundred times.
Subsequently, having sprinkled water upon the ground designated as Prasādi, as well as upon the Liṅga and the ashes,
one should not meditate on anything else, but should remember Him alone.

Having gazed upon the desired linga according to the rite of ten-fold concentration, one should perform the lustration ceremony with devotion and recite: "O Rudra, that which is yours... (Yā te rudra). || 26 ||
Having placed sacred ash upon the *liṅga* at the site of the *prāṇa-liṅga*,
one should indeed cast a consecrated flower before the *liṅga* while reciting the root mantra.
One should indeed offer water for the feet (pādya), the respectful oblation (arghya), and water for sipping (ācamana) using the respective waters from those vessels;
having bathed the Liṅga with the very water remaining in the vessel of renunciation (tyāgapātra).
Having taken [the water] with the support-vessel and sprinkled it upon one's own head,
one should respectfully wipe it away with a cloth while reciting the mantra beginning with "āvahanti."
Having placed his feet upon the ash-seat of the *liṅga* while meditating [on it], he should prostrate, worship, and offer water for the feet using the water from the vessel of knowledge. (30)
Having offered this water and taken it up with the supporting vessel while bowing low,
one should drink it after consecrating it with the mantra "kadrudrāya," uttering the words "ṛtam."

Then, having adorned the base of the *liṅga* with perfumes and other offerings, one should perform the *nīrājana* rite known as "the Occasion" (*avasara*) with the mantra, "He who is Rudra is indeed the Blessed One, and he who is Agni," and then offer fruits and other gifts.
Having offered this vessel of bliss, one should take it from the supporting vessel;
having offered it and consumed [the contents], one should place that vessel face down.

Then, having offered water for sipping (ācamanīyaka) with the water contained in the vessel for sipping, [he offers] water from the vessel for the ritual offering (tyāga-pātra) with the mantra "tatsavitur... (RV 3.62.10).
Then, having consecrated that water with the Rudra-hymns beginning with "Namaḥ," one should likewise sprinkle it upon one's own head with the mantra "Namaḥ śambhave."
(88) "Bringing [the deity]," having wrapped the image of the desired deity with a cloth and placed it upon a seat of ashes, one should receive the water from washing its feet.
Then, having brought smokeless embers, one should heat [the vessel] with this mantra:
"He who is Rudra is the Blessed One, and he who is Agni. (37)
According to the mantra, "He who is Rudra is indeed the Blessed One, and he is that which is space," one should offer me this enchanting incense, honored with its ten ingredients.
Then, saying "Be inflamed," he should show the one called the auspicious [mark];
and saying "He who is the spider," having given a pair of garments, he should smear ashes mixed with water using the mantras beginning with "Agni. (39)
One should offer the sacrificial thread while reciting "namo harikeśāya," and one should offer scents along with unbroken grains (akṣata) while reciting "gandhadvārām. || 40 ||
The wise one should apply fragrant unguents with the mantra "Umāsahāyam," and he should offer the scattering of unbroken rice grains (akṣata) with the mantra "Ākāśāt. (41)
O Maheśvarī, reciting "Without hands or feet" and "The golden vessel," one should display the lustration rite known as Karpūra.
Reciting "Tadevarta," one should offer flower garlands;
with "Namo hiraṇyabāhave," one should adorn [the deity] with a crown and other ornaments.
"O Rudra, that auspicious form of yours which is auspicious and a healing balm for all days"—
with these words, O Maheśvarī, one should offer the *nīrājana* known as *śṛṅgāra*.
With the mantra "Nidhanapataye" repeated a thousand times as the essence of the Veda, one should also offer flowers and leaves with the root mantra. || 45 ||
One should offer bilva fruits with the mantra "tad āditya," ashes with "yo vai rudra," and a white umbrella with "nama īśvarāya. || 46 ||
Having recited "Namo vātyāya," one should offer a fly-whisk;
with the mantra "Candramā manasaḥ," one should fan [the image] with a palm-leaf fan. || 47 ||
Reciting "sa yaścāyaṃ puruṣaḥ," he should offer a mirror;
reciting "yo vedādau," he should offer the sound of a bell. || 48 ||
Reciting "adhyavocat," he should then offer the sound of a conch shell;
likewise, he should cause the song "śivena vacasā tvā" to be heard.
Reciting "asau yo 'vasarpati," he should perform a dance;
with his left hand, he should indicate the sun rising and setting, while devoutly performing circumambulations of my Liṅga on all sides. (50)
Reciting "Salutation to the Blue-necked One" and indeed "Salutation," and reciting "Salutation to the Elder," one should perform the hymn of praise with undistracted mind. (51)
One should offer incense with the mantra "divyā mānuṣo gandhaḥ," and likewise perform the great lustration ceremony (mahānīrājana) with the mantra "na tatra sūryo bhāti."
One should light the hand-lamps while reciting "īrāṃ vahata," and one should also light the lamps while reciting "jyotiṣmatīm."
Those objects fashioned from rice flour in the likeness of hand-drums (ḍamaru) are called "luminaries" (jyotīṃṣi), and they are indeed pleasing to me.
Reciting "yā te rudra," one who is single-minded should make a request;
then one should perform the petition with "ajāta" and so forth.
With "vedāntavijñāna," one should offer flowers and other articles of worship. || 55 ||
If, at the time when the offering is due, many leaves, flowers, and so forth remain before the chosen *liṅga*, they shall fall upon the food items. (56)
That offering (nivedana) should be such that it is unfit for contact with the remains of previous offerings (nirmālya).
One should discard only the small remainder of it; one must not leave the linga with its top exposed.
Therefore, in the place called Śaraṇa, having scattered water and ashes over the food items with the Sāvitrī along with the Vyāhṛtis, [he should say]: "Fire is present in these food substances. (58)
Having sprinkled [the remains] with water using the Sāvitrī and the Rudra-gāyatrī mantras in this manner,
one should then offer the Svāhā-oblation to them, as well as to the Ācāra-liṅga and others. O beloved, listen to the specific procedure regarding the offering of the six liṅgas.
In this place of devotion, which is endowed with the power of action (kriyāśakti) and located at the nose,
known as the Ācāra-liṅga and consisting of the face of Sadyojāta,
one should offer the prasāda of fragrance with true devotion by means of the hand of the mind.
In the place of Maheśvara, at the seat of Jñānaśakti, in the limb of Rasanā,
specifically in the face of Vāmadeva known as Guruliṅga,
one should offer the *ruci* (desire) with the hand of the intellect through steadfast devotion. 61.
On this ground known as Prasādin, endowed with the power of Icchā (will),
and further at the Gaṅgaka site called Aghoramukha which bears the name of the Śiva-liṅga,
one should offer the form with devotion, attentiveness, and ego-sense. (62)
In the place of the Prāṇaliṅgin, which is joined with the primordial Śakti (Ādi-Śakti) and is the limb of the skin,
known as the Cāraliṅga and located in the mouth of Puruṣa, one who is firm in his vow should,
with devotion born of direct experience, offer the touch by means of the hand of the mind.
In the sanctuary, which is endowed with supreme power and connected to the sense of hearing, one should offer the "purification by sound" (śabdaprasādaka) at the Prasāda-liṅga facing the northeast;
this should be presented with the hand of true knowledge and through blissful devotion. || 64 ||

In the state of unity, however, one should offer one's resolve with devotion— characterized by the hand known as *sadbhāva* and called *samarasa*— into the Great Liṅga at the mouth of Paraśiva, which is endowed with the power of consciousness (*cicchakti*) and possesses the limbs of the mind. (65)
Thus, having correctly understood the limb, the sign, the devotion, the power, as well as the place, the face, the hand, and the grace, one should indeed worship properly; in this manner,
one should always practice the true state of offering.
(93) Dedication is of two kinds.
It is said that dedication is twofold: the limb of worship and the perpetual [dedication].
One should have devotion toward the act of dedication and the limb of worship through one's inner feeling, and not otherwise. (67)
In the place called Śaraṇa, the offering likewise consists of six stages;
however, in the stage of Unity (Aikya-sthala), one should place a flower upon the Liṅga with the root mantra.
Having offered incense, one should then present the *anandana-nīrājana* while reciting the mantra, "From which words turn back... (Taittirīya Upaniṣad 2.4.1). 69.
Reciting "sa viśvakṛt," he should offer betel;
then, beginning with "ārabhya," he should offer the betel and the lustration (nīrājana).
Chanting the two mantras beginning with "yo brahmāṇam" and "īśānaḥ," one should indeed offer the "mantra-flower" consisting of a multitude of flowers.
Then, reciting the mantra beginning with "asaṃkhyātāḥ sahasrāṇi," he should also offer the nīrājana known as "asaṃkhyāta. || 72 ||
Having covered the liṅga with a cloth while reciting the mantra "so'bravīt," one should place it carefully inside a casket while reciting "aṇoraṇīyān."
(94) Thus has the great worship, O Great Goddess, which yields great fruit, been proclaimed.
Having worshipped according to this rite, one shall not be subject to rebirth.
O Queen of Gods, listen as the specific procedure for the worship of the Guru is now told. (74)
Regarding the specific details of the worship of the Guru:

the [rituals] known as the flower-offering (padya), the water-offering (arghya), and the sipping of water (ācamana), as well as the renunciation, the knowledge, and so forth, do not exist here; there are only two vessels. (75)
The auspicious pitcher and the common vessel for the arghya offering are present;
everything else has been declared to be the same. What more do you wish to hear from this? || 76 ||

Thus ends the seventh chapter, titled "The Procedure for the Worship of Śiva," in the Kriyāpāda of the *Śrīkāraṇāgama*, within the dialogue between the venerable Pārvatī and the Supreme Lord (Parameśvara) in its latter portion. || 7 ||
(95) The eighth chapter. The Goddess said:
O God of gods, Lord of the world, you who are intent upon bestowing grace upon all!
This is the most excellent ritual procedure, endowed with Vedic mantras. || 1 ||
The proper duties to be performed by those entitled to the Vedas have been clearly elucidated;
now learn from me by what rule women, and especially the principal among them, may attain their life's purpose.
Mahādeva said:
O Mahādevī, I shall proclaim the tantric sequence of worship,
by the performance of which all may become recipients of all goals.
Regarding the sequence of Tantric worship:
among the Vidyās, the Śruti is supreme; within the Śruti, the Rudraikādaśinī is supreme; therein, the five-syllabled mantra; and therein, the two syllables "Śi-va. (4)
Therefore, whether one is authorized in the Veda or not authorized therein, worship performed with my root-mantra is superior in every respect. (5)
Alternatively, worship is even more distinguished when performed with Tantric mantras;
O beautiful lady, in these [mantras], every ritual service (upacāra) is clearly manifest.

But in the case of Vedic mantras, it is solely on the basis of figurative indicative power (*liṅga*) that those various mantras of the Veda are employed in their respective figurative applications. (7)
When those works in which the matter to be practiced is clearly revealed are being studied, the mind becomes devoted to that task.
Since I am attainable through devotion, worship performed without devotion is in vain;
therefore, O Goddess, those mantras of the Tantras are the most excellent of all for the purpose of worship.
In the Tantric worship, everyone has the right;
O fair-faced one, everyone has the right to the Tantras—whether they be Vaidikas or others, women or men, O lady of excellent vows. (10)
A Vedic practitioner may also perform the worship of the Śiva-pitcher (śivakumbha) in conjunction with Tantric rites;
he should worship the Śiva-pitcher with the mantra "Īśāna". || 11 ||
Īśāna is at the front of the jar, Tatpuruṣa likewise in the east; Aghora is in the south, and Sadyojāta in the west.
Vāmadeva is in the north, and Paramaśiva is in the center;
in the lower part is Parā Śakti, who causes the manifestation of the universe.
The form of the jar is of the nature of existence (sat), its luster is of the nature of consciousness (cit);
the water situated within it is supreme, the most excellent among all sacred fords (tīrtha).
"Consciousness-bliss (cidānanda-rasa) is directly known as the very form of Śiva.
Thus, one should worship the Śiva-vessel with mantras, perfumes, and other offerings. || 15 ||
O eternal abode of compassion, dwelling in the cave of the mountain of my heart,
please sit upon the seat of my hands today to accept this worship of your chosen liṅga.
With this mantra, one should place the desired liṅga within the lotus of the hand.
O You who are enriched by the fivefold play of Your own nature, O You who are intent upon the fivefold cosmic functions;
having been invoked, being well-pleased, remain ever present here.
Having thus invoked the gurus, bowed to them, praised them, and worshipped them in due order,
one should meditate upon me as being truly well-pleased and also recite the root mantra.
And having gazed upon the Liṅga for a long time according to the method of the ten-fold concentration (daśāvadhāna). || 18 ||
O Sadāśiva, O Lord, whose auspicious limbs are embraced by Sarvamaṅgalā and who touches the heart, accept this lustration offering with affection. 19.
One should perform the lustration ceremony with the mantra "nīrājanaṃ sānurāgam," and then,
having placed ashes and flowers [upon the deity], one should do so with the root mantra.
O Sadāśiva, O Īśa, you who abide within and pervade all that is outside, whose nature is the Jyotirliṅga; accept this waving of lights (nīrājana), which is known as the vision [of You].
Having thus performed the lustration rite (nīrājana) with the vision [of the deity], one should offer water for the feet (pādya). || 21 ||
O Supreme Lord, whose feet are honored by the crest-jewels of the foremost gods headed by Hari, please accept this water for washing the feet at your lotus-like feet.
Having thus offered the water for the feet, one should offer the arghya water into the hands.
O Lord of Girijā, whose lotus-like hands are marked with the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness and who protect your servants, accept this water-offering from my hands that are trembling.
Having thus offered the arghya, one should then offer water for sipping (ācamanīya) to the mouth. || 23 ||
O Lord, whose radiant throat is like a flock of crows seeking prey upon the world,
please accept this water for rinsing the mouth offered at Your glorious lotus-face.
Having thus offered water for sipping (ācamana), one should bathe the desired liṅga.
Obeisance to you, whose head is adorned by contact with the waves of the Gaṅgā;
O Supreme Lord, accept this bath of pure water. || 25 ||
Having bathed [the deity] in this manner, one should then pour the sacred water (tīrtha) over one's own head;
then, having taken the water from the feet (pādodaka), one should immediately offer salutations.
The service of the lotus feet of Śambhu is the most auspicious of all auspicious things, the purifier of all purifiers, and the bestower of all accomplishments for men.
Having thus consumed it, one should then worship the liṅga with perfumes and other offerings.
O you whose form is consciousness, the support of the universe, gross and subtle, higher than the highest, O Sadāśiva, Lord, accept this waving of lights known as the *avasara* offering. 28.

Having thus offered the *nīrājana* known as the "Opportunity" (*avasara*), and having presented fruits and other offerings before the chosen *liṅga*, one should sprinkle flowers and other items with ashes.
Having offered the ritual bath and the lustration ceremony (nīrājana), one should thereafter show [the deity] the mirror-image.
O Sadāśiva, sovereign of the ocean of perfect consciousness and bliss, O Lord,
accept this beautiful lustration rite known as the ceremonial bath.
Having thus given water for the feet, the respectful offering (arghya), and water for sipping,
and having presented these with the previous mantras, one should then provide the bath.
O You whose sense-bases consist of the five Brahmās, O You who are intent upon the fivefold cosmic acts,
O You who are affectionate toward Your devotees, please accept this bath of the five nectars.
O Lord of the World, accept this bath of pure water, radiant with the mass of matted locks bound by the river flowing through the sky. (33)
Having thus performed the consecration, one should pour the sacred water (tīrtha) upon one's own head;
then, having taken the water from the feet (pādatīrtha), one should pay homage with great reverence.
Salutations to you, the boat for crossing the ocean of existence, the cause of liberation, the means for the pacification of sins, and the sacred water of your feet. || 35 ||
O you whose nature is the supreme light that illuminates all lights without exception,
perform this heating of the coals to dispel the cold.
Thus, having arranged for the heating by means of smokeless fire, [he spoke].
O Śambhu, who are the self-manifestation that uproots all latent impressions without exception, O you who are affectionate toward your devotees, please accept this fanning with incense.
Having fanned the incense in this manner, one should again spread forth the incense.
O Lord Sadāśiva, accept this auspicious lustration ceremony (nīrājana), which acts as a jewel-mine for the infinite gems of the qualities of auspiciousness.
Having thus offered the auspicious *nīrājana* ceremony, one should present a garment. || 38 ||
O Śambhu, Lord of the Universe, who are clothed in an upper garment of human-skin and adorned with an elephant-hide, please accept this pair of garments.
Having offered a pair of garments, one should then maintain prosperity in this manner. || 39 ||

"O Lord of the worlds, let this ash, born from the fire of Śiva, which adorned the body of Pradyumna when it was consumed by the fire of the plowshare, be worn. Having thus resolved, he took up the cow-dung-derived ash mixed with water.
O Lord of Sacrifice,
O Ishvara, accept this golden sacrificial thread, which is like a sacred thread of serpents shining with the light from the jewels upon their hoods.
Having offered the sacred thread with this mantra, one should present the fragrant paste.
O you whose beautiful limbs are radiant with the application of smiles that are the very essence of desire—
accept this fragrant, glorious unguent associated with the moon.
Having thus offered perfume along with unbroken grains of rice, one should smear [the image] with that.
O Lord, who bestows inexhaustible limbs and maintains imperishable bliss;
O You worshipped by the vehicle of birds, please accept these unbroken grains.
Having thus offered white unbroken rice grains, one should then light camphor.
O Sadāśiva, O Īśa, accept this lustration known as camphor, radiant with the lustration offered by the rows of jewels from the necks of the celestial damsels.
Having thus offered the camphor lustration (karpūra-nīrājana), one should present a garland.
O Lord of Gods, whose body is adorned by the garlands of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and the host of Kapālas, accept this flower garland, as beautiful as a fine web of blossoms.
Having thus offered the garland, one should then present the ornaments.
O Lord, adorned with earrings of serpents whose crests are like millions of crescent moons,
O One praised by the world, accept these golden ornaments.
Having thus adorned her with ornaments blazing with various jewels. || 46 ||
O Sadāśiva, O Lord, who are beheld by the world through the sweet play of your love for Bhavānī, accept this waving of lights known as Śṛṅgāra. 47.
Having thus performed the lustration rite (nīrājana), one should worship with leaves and flowers,
using either the eight names or one hundred and eight.
O Lord, who are adorned with flower-like chariot wheels and are intent on slaying the one whose weapon is the flower (Kāma), accept these various kinds of flowers; salutations be unto you!
Having thus worshipped with flowers, one should offer bilva leaves.

(103) O you who possess beautiful ears like a coiled cow's ear, accept this most splendid *druparṇaka*— the *trisuparṇa* hymn, which flashes with color, was practiced by Śrī, and is exceedingly beautiful.
Having thus offered a bilva leaf, one should scatter ashes over everything.
O Lord, adorned with a crown of matted locks and the serpent Ananta as a parasol,
accept this white umbrella, beautifully embellished with strings of pearls.
Having thus offered the parasol, one should then offer the two chowries.
Fanned by the two chowries rising from the lotus-hands of Brahmā and Viṣṇu, I fan you with these two chowries; be gracious, O Abode of Compassion!
Having fanned him with two chowries, one should fan him with a palm-leaf fan.
O you whose mind is delighted by the discipline of keeping time with rhythmic clapping,
O abode of the color of compassion, fan me with the palm-leaf fan!
Having fanned him with a palm-leaf fan, one should also show him a mirror. || 53 ||
O you whose form is difficult to behold, today I show you a mirror with a surface as pure as a polished lens and cheeks as radiant as a shining mirror.
Having thus shown the mirror, one should offer the sound of the bell.
O you whose lotus-like hand is beautified by a bell shimmering with the nature of *nāda*, I cause the sound of the bell to be heard;
O you who are the form of *nāda*, hear what is pleasing.
Having offered the sound of the bell in this manner, one should then blow the conch shell.
Surrounded by hosts of lords of the Gaṇas intent on the act of blowing conchs,
O Lord, listen to the sound of the conch, which is as beautiful as a conch-shell neck.
Having thus sounded the conch, one should likewise cause the song to be heard.
O you who are intent on hearing the songs of Kambala and Aśvatara,
I shall now cause you to hear this song concerning your own wondrous life-story.
Having caused the singing to be heard, he should then cause the instrumental music to be heard. || 57 ||
O Śambhu, who are delighted by the sound of the great drum played by Murāri,
and who are fond of the resonance of the hand-drum (ḍamaru), please let me hear the music.
Having thus sounded musical instruments, one should then properly perform the dance. || 58 ||
O Great Dancer, expert in the great *tāṇḍava* arising from the abundance of your own bliss, perform your dance today; behold it! (59)
Having thus offered the dance consisting of gestures with the hand,
one should then offer a circumambulation with the fist joined by the thumb.
O you who are served by the gods, beginning with Brahmā, and who are intent upon the act of circumambulation;
O treasury of compassion, I perform three circumambulations—please accept them.
Having performed three circumambulations, one should pay homage many times.
Homage, homage to the progenitor of the daughter of the mountain king; homage, homage to the one whose mind-source has been reduced to ashes.
Homage, homage to the son born of the trained sun; homage, homage to the one who adorns the cool state.
Having thus offered salutations, one should thereafter perform a hymn of praise.
Salutations to you, the God of gods— the Brahman among Brahmins, the protector among protectors,
and the destroyer among even those who destroy.
Having performed the praise, the wise one should then perform the fanning with incense.
O Śambhu, whose body is enveloped by the incense of smoke from the burning of the great cremation ground, O lover of your devotees, please accept this fanning with incense. 64.
Having fanned the incense repeatedly and likewise having extended the incense smoke,
and having also kindled the great lustration lamp (mahānīrājana), one should offer it.
May there be auspiciousness for Mahādeva, who is the cause of all auspiciousness, whose very self is embraced by all that is auspicious, and whose name is uttered for the sake of auspiciousness.
May there be auspiciousness for her who has the form of the chosen *liṅga* and who grants all desired boons. || 66 ||

May there be auspiciousness for the Prāṇaliṅga, which exists in the vital breaths and within the mind in the form of a luminous liṅga, and which is the very nature of the knots of the vital breaths. (67)

May there be auspiciousness for You, who are perceivable through meditative states, who are full, who are the sole cause of both existence and non-existence, who perform the creation of the cosmic parts, and whose characteristic mark is all that exists.
Having performed the great lustration ceremony (mahānīrājana), one should immediately thereafter make a formal request.
I beg, I beg—the sweet name constantly from your speech;
I beg, I beg—the composition of your being constantly within my mind;
I beg, I beg—O Śiva, devotion to your lotus feet.
I entreat you, I entreat you—again and again, I constantly entreat that very same one. || 69 ||
There is no higher bliss to be attained than liberation—bliss that is free from sorrow and unshakable.
Grant me Your state swiftly; I know of no other supreme object of prayer.
Having thus made this request, one should then perform the formal petition. 70.
"According to the principle that the offenses of servants are pacified by prostration, I therefore bow down;
O Ocean of Compassion, forgive my transgressions."
Having made this request, one should then sprinkle the offering.
(107) We worship that most excellent and worthy refuge, the splendor of the divine Savitṛ, which from its very nature impels our thoughts toward the goal. 72.
Having thus sprinkled the offering, one should sprinkle it all around;
having performed the sprinkling, one should perform the offering of the six marks (ṣaḍliṅgārpaṇa).
O Sadāśiva, accept this lustration known as "Bliss," offered to the ocean of the nectar of consciousness and bliss, which is beyond the reach of speech and mind.
Having thus offered the lustration ceremony (nīrājana), one should also present betel-leaf.
O you who are distant from the activity of the three qualities, yet endowed with the three qualities;
accept this betel leaf with camphor, honored by ascetics.
Having thus offered the betel-leaf, one should then present the lustration ceremony (nīrājana). || 75 ||
O Lord Sadāśiva, eager to receive the betel-roll brought by Mother Ambikā from her lotus-like hand,
accept this lustration rite known as betel.
Having thus performed the lustration ceremony (nīrājana), one should then offer the flower of mantra (mantrapuṣpa).
O Lord, worshipped by endless handfuls of flowers from Viṣṇu and the other gods,
accept this handful of flowers, O destroyer of the one whose weapon is flowers (Kāmadeva).
Having thus offered a handful of flowers, one should present an incalculable number of lustrations (nīrājana).
O Sadāśiva, surrounded by thousands of countless forms of Śrīrudra, accept this incalculable lustration rite (nīrājana).
Having offered incalculable numbers of lustration rites (nīrājana), one should wrap [the image] with a cloth.
O you whose universal form is concealed by your own essential nature, as a cloth is by its threads, I envelop you with this garment; O desired form of the Liṅga, salutations be to you!
Having thus wrapped it with a cloth, one should place it carefully inside a casket. || 79 ||
O eternal abode of the hearts of true devotees, O refuge of the world, I enshrine You within my heart; dwell there happily, O companion of the virtuous!
"One should place [the deity] within the casket; thus has the great worship been described. (80)
This sequence of worship for married women (suvāsinīs) may be performed as an adoration of the Guru without vessels for water for the feet and other offerings;
alternatively, it may be abbreviated by employing the essential elements of worship appropriate to the occasion.
This is the primary method for the easy propitiation of married women. || 81 ||
This ritual procedure for worship has been declared according to the Tantras;
everything has been stated in brief. What do you wish to hear after this?

Thus ends the eighth chapter, titled "The Description of the Ritual for Tantric Worship," in the Kriyāpāda of the Uttara-bhāga of the Śrī-Kāraṇāgama, within the dialogue between Pārvatī and the Supreme Lord.
(110) Ninth Chapter. The Goddess said:
O Lord of the Lords of Knowledge, Great God, Omniscient One, Teacher of the Directions, All-pervading One!
"By hearing the ritual for worship from your own mouth, I have achieved my purpose. (1)
I desire to hear the rules specifically for those who are initiated;
O Lord, tell me them all, and protect me, O Compassionate One! (2)
Mahādeva said:
"Listen, O auspicious lady, I shall declare all the observances (niyamas) for one who is intent on my worship and desires my grace."
For those who have been initiated,
the leaves, flowers, wicks, and likewise the recitation of mantras must always be accepted according to the prescribed number and rule, and not otherwise.
Water and other substances touched by persons devoid of the purificatory rite of initiation (dīkṣā) must not be employed in rites such as those dedicated to me through offerings and the like. || 5 ||
At the time of worship, one should not look upon those who have not received the purificatory rite of initiation;
one should not become angry, one should not think of others, and one should not engage in conversation with others.
One should never separate the *liṅga* from one's body, the sacred ash from one's face, the *rudrākṣa* from one's neck, nor one's own name from one's speech. (111.7)
One should not use clothing, ornaments, flowers, food, drink, or medicine without first offering them to me, even if one’s life-breaths have reached the throat.
What has been offered to another, one should not offer to me;
and what has been dedicated to the Liṅga, one should not dedicate to another.
The Goddess said:
"If it is so, O Maheśāna, how can this be for women?
For it is taught that a wife must always consume the remains of her husband's meal."
But it was stated by you yourself that food should not be offered [to one who is impure]. || 10 ||
For this was formerly offered by the husband for his own linga;
how then could it be offered again, or even consumed, without being offered [to him]?
Cut through this doubt of mine, O abode of the ocean of compassion. || 11 ||
Mahādeva said:
"Well asked by you, O Goddess! Listen, my dear, for this is a secret. There is a specific distinction regarding the offering; I shall explain it, so be attentive."

The food offering (*naivedya*) is of two kinds: that which consists of the enjoyment of the *liṅga* and that which consists of permission (*anujñā*). [This is] the grace (*prasāda*) of my Guru, which takes the form of the remains of the Master (*bhartṛśeṣa*), and so forth.
Indeed, the offering of the sacred site (tīrtha) is said to be in the form of permission alone. || 13 ||

Indeed, through the application of karma, embodied beings constantly obtain enjoyments distinguished as desirable and undesirable; yet, even amidst those very things, one who observes my vow remains detached.

In the case of what is desired, one should perform the offering in the form of enjoyment; in the case of what is undesired, in the form of permission; and likewise in the case of sexual intercourse and similar acts.
The Goddess said:
"If the remnant belonging to the husband were not to be employed through the nature of offering enjoyment, then such an offering would indeed be broken for women every day. (16)
Since it has been declared that the remains of one's master should be consumed daily, how then could one offer them after having performed worship? (17)
If the remnant of her husband's meal is not fit for a devoted wife to eat with another person, then tell me, should she eat one or the other of those two, or both? (18)
Mahādeva said:

Even when a married woman (suvāsinī) has been worshipped, the offering of enjoyments and forms should be performed by another; having obtained her permission, that [offering] becomes the remnant for the husband.
And one should enjoy both [of these], O beloved, being endowed with devotion toward me.
That which is not offered to Me is unfit to be eaten, yet that which is offered to Me must not be abandoned;
he who rejects My grace does not deserve My grace.
The Goddess said:
"If it has been offered and must not be discarded, how is this possible?
How should this favor be given to wives and to disciples? (21)
How can water be given to those who seek it from the Raurava hell?
How could such things as rinsing the mouth or washing the hands possibly be accomplished there? (22)
Indeed, the discarding of the *prasāda* during acts such as rinsing the mouth is certainly conceivable;
however, since the *prasāda* is sacred, how can it serve for the purification of the mouth? (23)
How can a mouthful of water be desired if it has not been offered? If it is offered, then how can that [act of rinsing] be logically established? (24)
(114) A great doubt, the sole object of our report, afflicts us;
having made all this known, deliver the host of devotees! (25)

Mahādeva said: O beautiful lady, by the giving of grace to those beginning with one's wife, and the giving of water to those suffering in hell, there is no fault whatsoever in the renunciation of what has been offered.
Since renunciation that is not based on scriptural injunction falls within the scope of prohibition, just as renunciation performed contrary to injunction is not a fault but indeed a merit. (27)
One should perform those various rites using water intended for acts such as rinsing the mouth and cleansing; performing them in this manner, one does not incur fault. (28)

Even though the temple is exceedingly pure, there is no fault in the unavoidable evacuation of excrement therein, as it is based on scriptural injunction regarding the necessity of cleansing the mouth. (29)
This [substance] which is employed by the Guru and others in the form of the three drops (kaṇa) is not held to be pure therein, because it lacks connection with saliva.
Constantly intent on my worship, with his consciousness dependent upon meditation of me, and engaged in the contemplation of my name, he should not remember other deities or the like. (31)
The Goddess said:
"For those who are solely devoted to the duties of their caste and stage of life,
the service of the sacred fires and other such rites are indeed performed daily, both regularly and on specific occasions."
O Lord, how can those [duties] be performed by those whose supreme devotion is fixed on you alone? (32)
Mahādeva said:
O beloved, even for one who serves only a king, the service of his minister and others does not incur blame for the servant, provided it is performed under the influence of that king's command. (33)
Likewise, for those devoted to me, due to the injunctions of my command and the Vedas, there is no fault in performing obligatory and occasional rites or in serving other deities. (34)
One should not, even with great effort, give the remnants of the cooked food prepared for the purpose of offering to me to those who are not devotees or to those of a different caste.
O Maheśvarī, the devotion of one who, though personally engaged in enjoyment, regards a person devoted to Śiva as inferior merely by words, is in vain. (36)
Therefore, a mortal endowed with devotion—
whether possessing a small or even a very small number of Rudrākṣas, sacred ash, or ornaments of the Liṅga— [attains the goal].
One should perceive everything without doubt as being of the most excellent form. || 37 ||
The Goddess said:
How can this be possible for those who are solely devoted to the system of castes and stages of life?
For a Brahmin, by virtue of his superiority, ought to be of a different caste [than his wife].
When cultivated, how could the boundaries of caste not be violated? || 38 ||
Mahādeva said:
A Brahmin should indeed honor those devoted to other castes with his mind alone; for by behaving otherwise, he incurs degradation from his caste. (39)
For the duty toward the caste-restrictions brings about the cessation of rebirth in lower states;
devotion that is complete, steadfast, and pure bestows liberation. || 40 ||
O beautiful one in every limb, if there should be a loss of devotion among those belonging to the castes and stages of life, they would attain a lower state in the end.
Therefore, O Beloved, for those whose souls are endowed with complete devotion in all its limbs,
the strict observance of the duties pertaining to caste and stage of life is considered fruitful.

Thus ends the ninth chapter, titled "Instruction on Observances," in the section on ritual action (*kriyāpāda*) within the dialogue between Pārvatī and the Supreme Lord, in the latter part of the glorious *Kāraṇāgama*.
Chapter Ten. The Goddess said:
Regarding those who belong to Śambhu, who are pure and constantly wear the *liṅga*—
When contact with impurity has occurred, and when contact with worldly people arises;
Tell me, how might there be an expiation for these various kinds [of offenses]? || 1 ||
Mahādeva said: Well asked, O Great Goddess, by you who desire the welfare of the world!
I shall describe the rules for expiation for those who are always attached to the limbs of the Liṅga.
For the *liṅga* is always pure, whereas the body is always impure;
therefore, having rendered it pure through the application of the purification of the six paths (*ṣaḍadhva*), [one should proceed].
The *liṅga* established here is therefore [pure] despite bodily defects;
O beautiful lady, the *liṅga* shall not be impure under any circumstances.
"O Adrijā, it has been determined that my liṅga must not be touched by those who are devoid of the purificatory rite of initiation (dīkṣā) and whose bodies are impure."
p. 119) Regarding the consecration (*pratiṣṭhā*), only one who has been initiated (*dīkṣita*) has the authority;
one who is uninitiated has no authority for the consecration, my dear.
It is promised that the consecration must be performed by those alone who have been initiated.
Otherwise, there would be the destruction of the kingdom; therefore, one should not have it performed by others.
Even if a twice-born man were authorized for worship for the sake of others,
nevertheless, due to his status as a "son of an unmarried woman," his Brahminhood would be lost.
Because he lacks the qualification for the office of an Ācārya, he is not entitled to perform the Pratiṣṭhā;
however, if he is endowed with the purificatory rites of initiation (dīkṣā), he is entitled to perform worship in stationary [liṅgas].
One should apply oneself to that which is conducive to the welfare of both oneself and others; of this there is no doubt.
Therefore, one who is perfected through the purificatory rite of initiation (dīkṣā) and possesses the union of the Liṅga and the body (liṅgāṅga-saṅga),
becomes authorized for the installation (pratiṣṭhā) by virtue of being worthy of worship by the world.
O Dear One, those whose limbs have been purified by Śaiva initiation do not incur any fault even when touching my beautiful Liṅga, regardless of their state.
One who is uninitiated becomes certainly defiled by touching the *liṅga*.
If the *liṅga* has been touched by those who are uninitiated, it must indeed be consecrated once more.
The Goddess said:
"For one who is overcome by sleep at night and tossing about on both sides, how can the fault be pacified while remaining beneath the *liṅga*? (12)
Mahādeva said: For a fault committed by touching the hands, feet, or other limbs of a fair-browed woman,
no other atonement is praised than bowing at the feet of her husband in the morning.
Likewise, at dawn, upon the attainment of awakening, my supreme prostration is the pacifier of all defects, appearing in the form of a touch to the eyes. (14)
The Goddess said:
"Even though one who bears the liṅga is constantly untouched by bodily defects, contact with the uninitiated is indeed possible in this world. (15)
In acts such as shaving and the like, contact with a barber is not forbidden even by those of lower castes, including Caṇḍālas and Śvapacas. (16)
"What kind of expiation occurs upon contact with those who bear sectarian marks?
Explain all of this, O you who are intent on the welfare of the world. (17)
Mahādeva said: (p.
121) One must certainly strive so that the touch of a shaven-headed person does not occur during the shaving of the linga and other such rites;
otherwise, there is indeed a supreme expiation required.
Upon touching a barber, a practitioner of the Liṅga must discard his Śiva-sūtra and likewise his Brahma-sūtra, and wear them anew.
And one should recite the five-syllabled Gāyatrī one hundred and eight times.
Upon touching the *liṅga* after it has been shaved, one must especially perform a sprinkling with the *Pavamāna* and other *sūktas*, as well as the *Śrīrudra*.
Upon being touched by people such as Caṇḍālas and others, one should remove two threads and sprinkle [the image] with the Pavamāna hymns and other mantras one thousand and eight times.
Having recited the Gāyatrī and the root mantra, one should subsist on food only at night. || 21 ||
In the event of contact with those who are uninitiated, whether they be of the same caste or of a different caste,
one should recite the root mantra one hundred and eight times for the pacification of that fault.
The Goddess said:
"What kind of expiation is prescribed for the interruption of worship at the [proper] time,
as well as for the omission of worship during times of distress, and likewise for the omission of recitation?"
In the absence of leaves and flowers, [one may offer] a fixed number of them. || 23 ||
Mahādeva said:

"In the case of an interruption in the worship, the root mantra should be recited one hundred and eight times; likewise, in the event of an omission in the ritual worship or the recitation of mantras, the root mantra should be recited one thousand times. (24)
O fair-eyed one, if fixed leaves and flowers are not available,
one should recite the root mantra one hundred and eight times for each individual item.
The Goddess said:
"If the *liṅga* should fall down from the hand due to the power of negligence, what indeed should be done then? Tell me the expiation (*prāyaścitta*). (26)
Mahādeva said:
When, through negligence, the liṅga should fall from one's own hand to the ground,
one should then pick it up and recite the root mantra one hundred and eight times.
And for those faults not mentioned here, which are constantly possible for one who considers himself pure,
the root mantra should be recited one hundred and eight times as an expiation.
The Goddess said:
"O Lord, if there should be the breaking or the loss of the linga given by my preceptor, what indeed should be done then? Out of compassion, please instruct me on that. (29)
Mahādeva said:
"Ah, O you of excellent vows, I shall tell you this secret, even though it is hidden:
having bound [the image] with resin (sarjarasa) after breaking it into two or three pieces,"
Having performed the ritual placement of the digits of reality (tattvakalānyāsa), one should worship without distinction.

But when the linga has been reduced to powder, one should place the subtle constituents (kalās) residing within it into another linga and maintain that linga, having received it again from the hand of the Guru.
Now listen, O beautiful one, to what must be done when the *liṅga* is lost: upon the disappearance of the *liṅga*, one's life-breaths should be abandoned through the yoga of devotion. (32)

If one is unable [to perform the ritual], one should give up one's life; otherwise, for a period of twenty-one days, fasting and reciting the root mantra, one should seek out the Liṅga with the help of people.
Indeed, as soon as one receives the *liṅga* with devotion, at that very moment one should worship the Guru and the devotees of Maheśvara according to one's ability. || 34 ||
If even then there is no attainment, one should cast off the vital breaths through the yoga of true devotion;
however, if one is unable to relinquish the life-breaths, [one may take] another *liṅga* from the hand of the Guru.

One should, without negligence, maintain that which is adorned by the previously drawn placement of the *kalās* of the *liṅgin*, and which is permeated by the placement of the six paths (*ṣaḍadhvan*). (36)
The Goddess said:
"O God of gods, O Mahādeva, once a new linga has been installed, if one should then wish to obtain the former linga, what should be done? Tell me. (37)
Mahādeva said:
Even upon perceiving the former *liṅga*, one should never abandon the new one that has been adopted;
for all its parts were previously infused into the new one.
Having presented that previous linga to the guru, one should cast it into the water.
The Goddess said:
"If one whose linga has been lost should give up his life, then tell me, how can that body—which is devoid of the linga and thus unworthy—be consecrated? (39)
If another mark were to be worn, the abandonment of life would be useless;
if it were not to be worn, then his body would remain unsanctified. (40)
However, a fault is observed in both cases for an embodied being whose signs have vanished;
O abode of the ocean of compassion, sever this doubt of mine. (41)
Mahādeva said:
For one who has abandoned their food and whose *liṅga* has perished, there is union with liberation at that very moment;
there is no misfortune from that abandonment of life. Now hear how the consecration (*saṃskāra*) is performed. (42)

Having properly joined another linga that possesses the ninefold placement of the arts (kalānyāsa) for drawing forth and restoring the lost linga, one should consecrate the body according to the prescribed rite.
Even though this small body was joined with a *liṅga* for the sake of ritual refinement (*saṃskāra*),
there was no loss of the vital breaths (*prāṇa*) for one who has attained liberation;
therefore, that *liṅga* should always be worn with vigilance as if it were one's own life-breath.
O Goddess of noble vows, I have told you everything, even the secret;
this must not be revealed by you to one who has no son nor to one who is not a disciple.

Thus ends the tenth chapter, titled "The Exposition of the Rules for Expiation," in the section on Ritual Practice (Kriyāpāda) within the dialogue between Pārvatī and the Supreme Lord (Parameśvara), in the latter part of the venerable *Kāraṇāgama*.
